newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura to be searched as early as Tuesday--Kyodo.
newsitem.headline: Nomura to be searched as early as Tuesday--Kyodo.

text.p: Prosecutors are expected to start searching the headquarters of Nomura Securities Co Ltd as early as Tuesday as part of investigations into a scandal over its suspected illegal payments to a corporate client, Kyodo news agency said on Tuesday.
Both the prosecutors' office and Nomura declined to comment on the report.
The raid will be a joint search with Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC), Kyodo said.
SESC spokesmen were not immediately available for comment.

Nomura said earlier this month that two of its directors, who subsequently resigned, had made apparently illegal deals and funnelled funds to a corporate client linked by Japanese media to a former "sokaiya" racketeer.

Sokaiya, often linked to "yakuza" crime syndicates, typically try to extort money from firms by threatening to expose dubious business practices or to disturb shareholders' meetings -- called "sokai" in Japanese. Nomura president Hideo Sakamaki resigned from his post on March 14 to atone for the scandal. He became an adviser to the company, and chairman Masashi Suzuki took over his position while retaining the chairmanship.
The SESC had said it was conducting an investigation into the matter and police had said they were gathering information on the case.
